newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks rally, no end yet to bull run.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks rally, no end yet to bull run.

text.p: Croatian stocks forged ahead on Thursday in another record-breaking session and traders saw no end to the bull run, which caught the market by surprise in a usually dead summer holiday season.

"Unlike last year, this summer has seen a growing number of more serious investors on the Zagreb Stock Exchange," said Nenad Pavletic of Auctor brokerage, referring to new foreign banks in Croatia which brought their investors along.
Foreigners are said to have been behind each of the three strong rallies the tiny bourse has experienced so far.

"Supply is quite good, as well as demand which centres in blue chips. They then pull the market up," Pavletic told Reuters. "Another reason could be the bourse's decision to lift comission fee on summer deals."

Of 19 active issues on Thursday, 12 rose, three fell, three closed flat and one traded for the first time, with three -- brewery Karlovacka Pivovara, drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka preference stock hitting new highs.
Volume rose to 25,898 shares, turnover more than doubled to 16.8 million kuna.
Karlovacka, majority owned by Chile's brewer Cervecerias Unidas, closed 50 kuna stronger at 650 -- two off its all-time peak earlier in the session. It sold 1,104 shares.
Karlovacka's last record of 610 kuna was set in early July and market participants saw room for its further growth due to a favourable price to earnings ratio.

Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka ordinaries closed 10 kuna higher at 2,410. They peaked at 2,447 on Wednesday after the dollar-boosted rise of their Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) in London. These eased to $37.25 from $37.875 at the open.
"I am quite optimistic about Zagrebacka. There are three market makers on the buying side and dollar has an upward trend," Pavletic said.
The other blue chip Pliva lost five kuna to 566, reversing its 10-day upward trend, but only after hitting another record of 572 kuna earlier in the day. It sold 600 units.
But ship repairer Viktor Lenac was seen as heading for a further correction and trading in 160-170 kuna range. It shed two kuna to 160 on volume of 165 shares.
In a semi-regulated market segment, Zagrebacka's preferred E-series jumped 110 kuna to 1,650 on volume of 211. It had set a previous 1,550-kuna record on Wednesday.
Market debutant Rijecka Banka was most actively traded, selling 16,913 shares at a nominal price of 100 kuna each in what traders believed to be a pre-arranged deal.
Top gainer hotelier Arenaturist climbed 32 kuna or 29.9 percent to 139 kuna, selling 100 units in a single deal.
Biggest decliner Dalmatinska Banka lost five kuna or 1.56 percent to 315 kuna with 680 shares sold. But its closing price was not seen as reflecting its true potential.

One trader pointed out a 345 kuna price recorded earlier in the day, which came despite the appointment of a new board president. The bank said in a statement this change would have no negative impact on its further activities.
